Day 1
From Hotel: 10 min · 4 min → Ping An Finance Centre
1.Ping An Finance Centre
Kohn Pedersen Fox's 599 m tower is the fourth-tallest building in the world, and the Free Sky deck on floor 116 puts you 541 m up behind a wall of glass — Futian's towers below, the container cranes west, and the hills of Hong Kong across the bay.

9 min → Lianhuashan Park
2.Lianhuashan Park
A wooded 150-hectare hill closing the north end of the Futian axis. A six-metre bronze of Deng Xiaoping stands on the summit, and behind it the city lines up exactly as it was planned — Civic Center, then the towers, then Ping An dead centre.

6030 Hongli Road · Futian
23 min → Nantou Ancient City
3.Nantou Ancient City
Shenzhen reads as a city with no past until you walk through this gate. Nantou was the seat of Xin'an County, which governed everything from Dongguan to Hong Kong; the site has been settled since 331 CE and the Ming ramparts went up in 1394. Lanes of shophouses, ancestral halls and a county office run behind the south gate.

3109 Shennan Avenue · Nanshan
16 min → Shenzhen Bay Park
4.Shenzhen Bay Park
Ten kilometres of seafront running the Nanshan and Futian coast, ending in the Mangrove Coastal Eco-Park — part of a reserve that feeds migratory birds on the East Asian flyway. Come for the last hour of light: the water goes still, the Nanshan towers turn to silhouette, and the far shore is Hong Kong.

Local Tastes
Shajing Oysters
Shajing in Bao'an has farmed oysters since the Song dynasty and the local ones are prized for plump meat and thin bellies. Eaten grilled over charcoal, or folded into an oyster pancake by stalls that have sold nothing else for decades.
Shajing Oyster Street · Li Ji Zhang Guang Oyster House
Gongming Roast Goose
A Cantonese roast that made its name in Bao'an's Gongming nearly a century ago: lacquered skin taken to a hard crackle over meat that stays juicy underneath, carved to order and served over rice.
Xia Cun Xin Qiang Ji Roast Goose Restaurant
Food Delivery
Meituan
Foreign number: not accepted. — The standalone app wants a +86 number at the OTP step; the Meituan mini-program inside WeChat rides the WeChat login and sends no code at all.
Meituan is the default in Shenzhen and its restaurant list is wider than anything else by a distance — most of Futian and Nanshan inside half an hour, with the rider tracked to the door. It runs in Chinese throughout, menus included, so budget time for translation and expect a Chinese-format address.
meituan.com
Ele.me
Foreign number: not required. — Reached as a mini-program inside Alipay, which already carries the sign-in and the card, so no separate verification code is ever sent.
Ele.me — folded into Taobao Instant but still called Ele.me by everyone — is Alibaba's answer to Meituan and the easier door for a visitor, because Alipay has already done the identity and payment work. The restaurant list thins out faster outside the central districts.
ele.me
Getting Around
DiDi
Foreign number: accepted. — The code arrives by SMS on foreign carriers; where it does not, the DiDi mini-program inside WeChat signs in on the WeChat account and skips the code entirely.
DiDi absorbed Uber's China business in 2016 and is the only ride app that matters here — coverage is total across Shenzhen and a car arrives in minutes. The app runs in English; the drivers rarely do. Set the destination by pin rather than by typing an address, and let the in-app translation carry the rest.
didiglobal.com

Guangzhou–Shenzhen–Hong Kong Express Rail Link → Hong Kong West Kowloon and Guangzhou South. The first underground railway station built under a Chinese city centre and the largest of its kind in Asia.

Heads Up
Ping An Finance Centre — Passport at the gate and an early cutoff
Free Sky books against your passport number and checks the physical passport at the gate. Last entry is 7:15pm, though the deck itself runs to 8:00pm.
Worth Knowing

A county town, a border, and half a kilometre of glass — all inside one day.

Shenzhen is sold as a city with no history, and the itinerary quietly disproves it. The walled town at Nantou was administering this coast roughly sixteen centuries before the first tower went up in Futian. The skyline is the young part; the county seat is not.

The view from Lianhuashan is not a happy accident. The park, the Civic Center and the tower beyond it sit on a single north–south axis, a planning device borrowed from imperial China and applied to a city built from scratch. Stand at the statue and you are standing at the top of a composition that was drawn before most of what you can see existed.

One pattern governs almost every app here: the standalone version gates on a Chinese mobile number, and the mini-program inside WeChat or Alipay does not. Ride-hailing is the exception that proves it, because DiDi takes a foreign number outright. Install WeChat and Alipay before the flight and most of the rest of the city opens up behind them.

The far shore at Shenzhen Bay is another jurisdiction. Hong Kong sits across the water from the mangroves, close enough to pick out buildings, and the Express Rail Link under Futian Station reaches West Kowloon — so the border is both the view at the end of the day and a short ride from the middle of it.
